topics.title: Stern Show Guests Discuss Carol King and Reed Savage
topics.summary: The Howard Stern Show hosts interview Carol King and Reed Savage, discussing their musical careers and personal lives with tangents about celebrity relationships, concert promotions, and awkward questions regarding physical appearances.

topics.title: Idaho Dreams & Carole King’s Album
topics.summary: Howard discusses Reed Savage’s self-sufficiency while comparing it to Johnny Carson’s children, then introduces Carole King’s new album. He speculates about living in Idaho with taekwondo lessons and a satellite dish, playfully suggesting a romantic relationship with King herself amidst discussions of marital transitions and potential infidelity.

topics.title: Rob Lowe’s Atlanta Phone Mishap
topics.summary: A chaotic radio interview spirals as hosts repeatedly misidentify Rob Lowe, initially confusing him with Carol King and later discussing his legal troubles involving a young woman in Atlanta. The conversation shifts to details of community service, the size of Lowe's penis, and attempts to connect Lowe with callers seeking dating advice before abruptly ending.

topics.title: Rob Lowe’s Video Tape Controversy
topics.summary: During the broadcast, hosts discuss a video tape featuring Rob Lowe and several young women, sparking concerns about impropriety and legal issues. The conversation shifts to Lowe's financial troubles – including an overdrafted bank account – and his attempts to finance new television specials while facing scrutiny from school officials regarding community service obligations.

topics.title: Moles, Handwriting, Government Art & Controversy
topics.summary: The program begins discussing a man who believes his intelligence resides in surgically removed moles. This transitions to an attempt to decipher Gary’s handwriting and subsequent frustration when it doesn't work. The segment then shifts unexpectedly to government funding of art galleries featuring graphic photographs that Senator Jesse Helms deems inappropriate, leading to discussions about artistic standards.

topics.title: Artistic Provocations and Government Funding Debate
topics.summary: A discussion unfolds regarding the definition of art and government funding, featuring provocative artworks including depictions involving a bull whip and urine. Participants question artistic merit while suggesting only works purchased by individuals qualify as genuine art, leading to heated exchanges about propriety and standards.
